rationale: This is a very small (339 lines, 12 functions, ~1.4 KB text) pointer- and recursion-heavy trie benchmark where measured runtime is a primary metric, so the table favors low-cost, high-coverage transforms: SUB gets the strongest security/diversity weights since instruction substitution is nearly free and effective across this arithmetic/logic-light but comparison-heavy code, while SPLIT and IGV are boosted as cheap enablers (SPLIT fattens basic blocks so FLA/BCF have more to flatten, IGV diversifies interprocedural structure across the 12 small functions at negligible runtime cost). FLA is moderately weighted because trie_insert/trie_scan/main contain the dispatch-rich control flow where flattening pays off, but its RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights keep it off trivial accessors; BCF is retained with elevated RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights so bogus control flow lands only on the few large, security-relevant functions (addfile, charsequence_push, trie_insert) rather than everywhere in an already size-constrained binary. ICALL and IBR carry higher runtime penalties since indirect calls and branch rebasing add per-execution cost on hot trie-traversal loops and are correctness-sensitive in this pointer-dense code, so they apply selectively where features justify them; CorrectnessRisk weights stay low overall because all seven passes are mature for C at this scale, with the highest reserved for FLA and ICALL on the recursive/pointer-manipulating trie routines.
